problem: The section first defines the load line as the line from the Thevenin side, V = Vth − I Rth. It then says 'Change RL and only the load line changes', which reverses that definition: the load line is fixed by Vth and Rth, and it is the load's own V–I characteristic (V = I RL) that changes when RL changes.
fix: Say: 'Change RL and only the load characteristic changes; the load line V = Vth − I Rth and hence Vth and Rth stay fixed. The new operating point is where the new load characteristic cuts the same load line.'

problem: The answer says 'The load is part of the resistance seen at the terminals', which clashes with the chapter's own warning that Rth is not the resistance of the circuit including the load. The load is outside the network; it only corrupts Rth if it is left connected while measuring.
fix: Say: 'If the load is left connected, the resistance measured at A and B includes RL in parallel with Rth, so the value found is not Rth. Remove the load, then look into the open terminals with the independent sources killed.'
